title: The Carbon Cycle
seo_title: Carbon Cycle Worksheets: Photosynthesis, Respiration and CO2 Data (High School Biology)
standard_text: Develop a model to illustrate the role of photosynthesis and cellular respiration in the cycling of carbon among the biosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, and geosphere.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on the carbon cycle (NGSS HS-LS2-5): reservoirs, photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, fossil fuels and Mauna Loa CO2 data. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Carbon moves; it is never used up.
key_sub: Photosynthesis takes CO2 out of the air; respiration and burning put it back.
body_html:
How to think about it

Carbon atoms move; they are never used up.

  • Photosynthesis takes CO2 out of the air; respiration and decomposition put it back.
  • Burning fossil fuels moves ancient carbon from rock into the air faster than it returns.
Example

Which process removes CO2 from the air?

Plants use CO2

Answer: photosynthesis

Example

CO2: 339 ppm in 1980, 414 ppm in 2020. Rise?

414 − 339

Answer: 75 ppm

Common mistakes

  • Thinking respiration removes CO2. It adds it.
  • Thinking carbon is used up. It moves between reservoirs.
  • Forgetting the ocean and rocks store carbon.

faq.q: What are the main carbon reservoirs?
faq.a: The atmosphere, the biosphere (living things), the hydrosphere (oceans and lakes) and the geosphere (rocks and fossil fuels).

faq.q: How do photosynthesis and respiration cycle carbon?
faq.a: Photosynthesis moves carbon from CO2 in the air into sugars. Respiration breaks the sugars down and returns CO2 to the air.

faq.q: Why is CO2 in the air rising?
faq.a: Burning fossil fuels and clearing forests add carbon to the atmosphere faster than plants and oceans remove it.

items.q: Which carbon reservoir holds wood in a living tree?
items.e: Wood in a living tree is part of the biosphere.

items.q: Is carbon used up in the carbon cycle?
c: No. Atoms move between reservoirs but are not used up.
items.e: Matter is conserved.
